title: Pressure injury stages

findings.where: Fact 4; step "stage3" caption and narration; STAGES[2], Frame description; images 1, 2, 5, 9, 10 and 13
findings.title: Stage 3 must exclude directly palpable deeper structures
findings.problem: The definition excludes exposed fascia, muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage and bone, but not directly palpable structures. A pressure injury with one of these structures directly palpable is Stage 4 even when it is not visible. The current Stage 3 wording therefore overlaps the stated Stage 4 criteria.
findings.fix: Change every Stage 3 definition to state that fascia, muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage and bone are neither exposed nor directly palpable.

findings.title: DTPI illustration places the entire deep lesion within dermis and fat
findings.problem: Fact 7 and the accessible description locate the initiating injury at the bone–muscle interface. DeepTissueStrip draws only epidermis, dermis and fat, with a closed damage ellipse ending inside fat and normal tissue beneath it. There is no cue that deeper damaged anatomy is cropped out. Although this could be intended as a superficial excerpt, that intent cannot be verified from the illustration.
findings.fix: Include muscle and bone and show representative deep damage at their interface with overlying skin changes, or explicitly mark the strip as a cropped view with deeper injury continuing below it. Do not imply that DTPI has a fixed staging depth.

assessment: Revise before publication. The Stage 3 definition omits a decisive Stage 4 discriminator, and the deep-tissue schematic does not match the stated injury mechanism.
